SpecTrace: Spec-Driven Development traceability for .NET Usage: dotnet spectrace [options] Commands: report Requirement → code → test matrix. --format md|json|github md by default; github = GitHub Actions annotations --link-base prefix for absolute links in md (PR comments) --out write to a file instead of the console --fail-on-gaps exit code 1 if active requirements are not implemented or not tested --fail-on-drift exit code 1 if there are unreviewed spec changes (spectrace.lock) lock Records the current version of the spec as reviewed (spectrace.lock). --requirement only that requirement (repeatable); without it, all active ones --check does not write: exit code 1 if there are unreviewed changes context Requirement context for an agent: statement, criteria, status and how to mark the work. scaffold-tests xUnit skeletons for criteria without tests. --project folder of the test project (required) --requirement only that requirement --namespace root namespace of the test project mcp MCP server over stdio for agents (Claude Code, VS Code, Agent Framework...). import speckit Imports GitHub Spec Kit specs (a spec.md or a specs/ folder). --prefix

ID prefix (default: initials of the feature, e.g. PA1) --out output (single feature only); default spectrace.spec.md next to the source import openspec Imports OpenSpec specs (openspec/, openspec/specs or a spec.md). --prefix

ID prefix (default: the capability name, e.g. AUTH) --out output (single capability only); default /
